verdict: Avoid new wholesale-trade exposure in Dimapur for now; lend only to established, GST-compliant distributors with tight stock-and-receivable controls, and decline cash-heavy, single-community-dependent traders.
title: Dimapur Wholesale Trade: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business actually is
**Dimapur wholesale trade is a stock-and-credit business, not a margin business.** A wholesaler buys fast-moving goods — food, garments, FMCG, building material — holds inventory in a godown, and sells on short credit to retailers across Nagaland and into Assam. Cash is made on turnover and supplier terms, not on price. **So when a proposal lands, check the stock turn and the receivable days first; if either is missing, ask for the last twelve months of purchase and sales ledgers.**

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in inventory and receivables, and both are the risk.** CRISIL flags obsolescence risk as high for garments and mobile phones, and treats receivables as a sizeable share of a trader's current assets [9][10]. **So take stock statements and an ageing of receivables every month; if receivables exceed the scale of operations, ask why and get the top-five debtor list.** Capex is light — godown and vehicles — so most of the loan is working capital.

## What has changed now
**The macro backdrop is tight: repo at 5.5%, raised from 5.25%, with RBI tightening [D].** Bank credit is running +29.1% YoY against activity +6.1% [D] — money is chasing trade faster than goods move. **Locally the tailwind is real: Nagaland GST collections are +13.8% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1% [D].** But the local press is thin and dated: the trade-expo story is from 2017 [1], and the pork-price story is from February 2024 [3]. **Treat local colour as stale; lean on first principles and the GST signal.**

## Who to pursue, who to avoid
**Pursue established distributors of FMCG and staples with GST-registered retail buyers and steady monthly turnover.** Peer evidence supports wholesale as a growing channel — Aditya Birla Lifestyle reported wholesale up 18% [7] — and commercial-vehicle demand is healthy [4]. **Avoid cash-sale traders, single-supplier dependents, and anyone exposed to garment or electronics obsolescence [9].** The ZCCI rejection of a business-closure directive [2] tells you local trade bodies are resisting pressure — a sign of friction, not stability.

## How to grow safely
**Structure as a cash-credit or bill-discount line against stock and receivables, not a term loan.** Take monthly stock statements, receivable ageing, and GST returns; covenant a minimum stock cover and a receivable-days ceiling. **If a borrower cannot produce GST returns matching declared turnover, decline.**
